tiles: What pure shape and contrast can carry
Six pieces I kept for their quiet confidence
challenge: The Bauhaus interests me because it treated design as a kind of thinking — shape, proportion, and balance taking on the weight that color or ornament might elsewhere. Taking the color out entirely was my way of testing whether I'd actually absorbed any of that.
approach: I read about the school and the people behind it, then drafted variation after variation in black, white, and gray, watching for the compositions where every form felt earned. I kept the ones that held their own without needing anything else to carry them.
result: Six pieces made it through — the ones where the restraint felt like a strength, not a limitation, and that I genuinely enjoyed looking at. They're available as prints in case the quiet confidence of a Bauhaus-minded piece appeals to someone else the way it does to me.
